title: Loss Assessments on Several Units from One Association Loss (CondoGuard)
content:
## Rule

1. When one association loss produces assessments on several units the customer owns, each unit's share is claimed only on the CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy of that unit, and each policy's loss assessment limit, deductible assessment sublimit and loss assessment deductible apply separately per unit.
2. One occurrence is one association loss date with one assessment basis. For one unit an occurrence is paid at most once, up to that unit's cap, however many assessment notices the association sends for it.
3. The amount already paid for an occurrence is the total of the loss assessment payments issued, and not voided, on the claims that share the same association loss date and assessment basis across the customer's CondoGuard policies.
4. A share already paid under one unit's policy is never paid again under another unit's policy, and the shares of units the customer does not own are never paid.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Same occurrence | Where the share is claimed |
|---|---|---|
| Two notices from the association for the same loss date and the same assessment basis | yes, one occurrence | once, on the policy of the unit assessed, up to that unit's cap |
| The same loss date, one notice on a master deductible share basis and one on another basis | no, two occurrences | each on the unit's own policy |
| One loss date, assessments on unit 4B and unit 7C, both owned by the customer | one occurrence per unit's policy | the 4B share on the 4B policy, the 7C share on the 7C policy, each with its own limit, sublimit and deductible |
| An assessment on a unit the customer does not own | not paid | nowhere |

## Example (hypothetical amounts)

A customer owns two units in one building, each insured under its own CondoGuard policy with a loss assessment deductible of 250 USD. One association loss date produces an assessment on each unit. The share of the first unit is paid on the first unit's policy with that policy's 250 USD deductible, and the share of the second on the second policy with its own 250 USD deductible; the first unit's share is never paid a second time on the second policy.
